name: MN-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by 18 points, among the reddest in Minnesota
Incumbent Fischbach holds a roughly 3-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price Osberg's chances at about 2%
No public polling and no outside spending signal a competitive race
model.rationale: An R+18 district with a well-funded incumbent leaves little room for an upset; markets price Fischbach near-certain, and even a national environment tilted toward Democrats does not plausibly close an 18-point partisan gap.
model.watch: A major scandal or a dramatic late national shift toward Democrats could narrow the margin, though the absence of polling in the district would make any such movement hard to detect.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minnesota's 7th District covers rural western Minnesota and leans Republican by about 18 points, one of the strongest GOP tilts in the state. Michelle Fischbach, the incumbent, is seeking another term and holds a clear financial edge, having raised roughly $1.6 million to Democrat Erik Osberg's $537,000. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Osberg about a 2% chance of winning. Osberg has raised a respectable sum for a district of this lean, but the structural advantages sit firmly with Fischbach, and outside groups have shown no interest in either side. The forecast expects her to win by a wide, double-digit margin, with a national environment that leans Democratic this year doing little to change the underlying partisan math.
